en: The Hymn to the Lord Buddha.
Om, homage to the Buddha!
To the Perfectly Awakened One, lotus-eyed, omniscient, and compassionate in nature.
I pay homage to the Teacher Samantabhadra, the Lion of the Śākyas. || 1 ||

I bow to Śrīghana, the glorious one, the most excellent, the mass of coolness, the bestower of auspiciousness, the illustrious, the creator of prosperity, the peaceful, and the embodiment of peace. || 2 ||
I bow to Indu, the proponent of selflessness, who is faultless, without support, learned in the Vedas, pure in soul, and free from grossness. (3)

I bow to the Tathāgata, who brings about cessation, whose knowledge is eternal, who is free from conceptual construction, who is constant, whose hair is like a treasure in the sky, and who is beyond all proliferation.
I bow to Viśveśvara, the knower of liberation, who possesses the form of the universe, the leader, the perfect Brahman of the universe, who is free from passion. || 5 ||

I bow to the Lord of the Universe, who is endowed with knowledge and conduct, whose splendor is stainless, who is free from sinking [into delusion], who possesses steadfastness, and who is devoid of ignorance.
I bow to the Sage, the son of Śuddhodana, the tamer of the untamable, the peaceful, the pure, the Sugata, the one of auspicious destiny, the gentle one of radiant fame. (7)

I bow to the Lord of Yoga, the One Possessed of the Ten Powers, the Knower of the World, the One Honored by the World, the Teacher of the World, the Embodiment of the World, and the Protector of the World. (8)
I bow to him who is the embodiment of gold, who is the stainless ocean of action, who possesses all the arts, whose form is beautiful,
who is the object of compassion, and who has the luster of gold.
I bow to him of great intelligence, great heroism, great wisdom, and great power; to him of great sacrifice, great fortitude, and mighty arms. || 10 ||
I pay homage to Amitābha, the primordial purifier, that Brahma, the unconquered and marvelous, the noble one who benefits others, the Protector. (11)
I bow to the God of gods, the Great God, the divine, the one who is worshipped, the imperishable, the embodiment of authority, the Lord of gods, who possesses a celestial form. 12.
I bow to the Blessed One, the ultimate reality, the supreme light, the highest Lord, the most excellent creator of existence and non-existence. || 13 ||
I bow to Śiva, the auspicious Śaṅkara, who has conquered the four Māras and the like, who knows reality, who is the essence of truth, whose conduct is ever-virtuous, and who is the caravan leader.
I bow to the Lord of Jinas, the supreme among men, who has conquered his senses and overcome all afflictions; the highest, the true state, Brahman, the field of merit. (15)
Having praised the best of sages with these [verses], men, freed from all taint, attain the divine and eternal state of liberation. || 16 ||
The wise person who, having risen early in the morning, constantly recites this hundred and eight pure names which destroy all sins— || 17 ||
He obtains his desired enjoyments, which are described as being accompanied by mental happiness;
even diseases do not afflict him, and his transgressions are destroyed. (18)
Endowed with long life, health, sovereignty, and complete liberation, as well as being wise and eloquent, he is born thus in birth after birth. (19)
The hymn to the Lord Buddha composed by Brahmā is completed.
